statusDetail: Coverage complete across 58 atomic checks and seven representative paths. Excluded duplicate tool templates and authenticated account/checkout internals; merge and compress represent the file-tool family.

page.framework: Server-rendered multi-page application with client-enhanced file workflows
page.notes: Public PDF utility, localized into many languages. Audited homepage, two tool entries, an end-to-end merge flow, pricing, login, Arabic RTL, and 404 recovery. Not covered: every duplicate PDF tool, authenticated account settings, payment checkout, or destructive document operations.

paths.description: Homepage and tool directory, representing the main discovery/listing template.
Primary PDF task from upload through ordering, merge processing, and successful download state.
A second file-tool template checked at a narrow viewport to represent the wider conversion/tool family.
Commercial plan comparison and FAQ template, including billing controls and account calls to action.
Authentication form checked for keyboard focus, input assistance, and invalid submission recovery.
Arabic localized homepage checked for translation, RTL direction, and mobile reflow.
Representative HTTP failure route checked for a useful error and recovery action.

findings.summary: The site ignores the user’s dark color-scheme preference.
findings.evidence: The dark-mode screenshot is pixel-identical to the light screenshot; computed body background remains rgb(245,245,250) and html color-scheme is normal.
findings.suggestedFix: Declare color-scheme: light dark and provide preference-driven surface/text tokens with prefers-color-scheme or light-dark().

findings.summary: The consent panel obscures primary content on every public page tested, especially on mobile.
findings.evidence: At 360x800 the 336px-tall panel covers the tool filters and cards; it appears on homepage, merge, compress, pricing, and 404 before interaction.
findings.suggestedFix: Use a compact, non-blocking consent notice; expose equally direct accept and reject actions without covering the primary task.

findings.summary: Consent controls are custom anchor-like elements rather than semantic dialog/buttons.
findings.evidence: The platform probe finds #ck_set and #okck as anchors without href, and no dialog/popover primitive exists.
findings.suggestedFix: Use a semantic dialog or appropriate popover with real buttons, keyboard focus management, and declarative dismissal.

findings.summary: Keyboard focus is not visibly indicated on primary controls.
findings.evidence: Programmatically focused login links, inputs, submit button, and merge picker all compute outline-style none and no focus box-shadow; some tested controls are only 40px tall.
findings.suggestedFix: Add a strong :focus-visible indicator that is not removed, and keep interactive targets at least 44 CSS px where possible.

findings.summary: Blank login submission provides no visible validation or recovery guidance.
findings.evidence: The before and after blank-submit screenshots are visually identical; fields remain without aria-invalid or error text.
findings.suggestedFix: Validate after interaction, identify each invalid field, focus the first error, and announce a concise summary through a live region.

findings.summary: Primary secondary templates miss the good LCP threshold in lab runs.
findings.evidence: Lighthouse measured LCP 3.3s on merge and 3.2s on pricing, while the homepage was 2.3s. CLS was 0 and TBT remained low.
findings.suggestedFix: Profile each LCP element, make it discoverable in initial HTML, prioritize only the actual LCP resource, and shorten its dependency chain.

findings.summary: Critical rendering depends on CSS/font chains and homepage LCP discovery is delayed.
findings.evidence: Lighthouse flags LCP discovery and dependency-tree insights; HAR identifies a parser-blocking stylesheet and five font files totaling 102KB.
findings.suggestedFix: Inline only critical styles, reduce font variants, use stable fallbacks, and ensure the LCP resource is discovered and prioritized from initial HTML.

findings.summary: Third-party analytics is the single largest script on the initial load.
findings.evidence: The HAR records GTM at 164,953 bytes, 31% of all 527,903 transferred bytes, larger than the 90,854-byte first-party bundle.
findings.suggestedFix: Load analytics only after an appropriate consent/state decision and use a smaller, conditional measurement path.

findings.summary: Core controls and pricing content have missing or invalid accessible semantics.
findings.evidence: Lighthouse finds an unlabeled merge file input, three pricing images without alt, and FAQ menuitem roles without required parents. Login inputs also have no labels.
findings.suggestedFix: Give every input a persistent label/name, use decorative empty alt where appropriate, and replace the FAQ menu pattern with semantic buttons/details.

findings.summary: Several primary controls narrowly fail WCAG text contrast.
findings.evidence: Lighthouse reports 4.35:1 white-on-red for Select PDF files and 4.22–4.25:1 consent actions, below 4.5:1; similar failures occur on pricing.
findings.suggestedFix: Darken the red and blue action colors enough to maintain at least 4.5:1 for normal text in every state.

findings.summary: Key templates lack a main landmark and contain invalid heading/FAQ structure.
findings.evidence: Lighthouse finds no main landmark on merge and pricing, skipped heading levels on pricing, and invalid menuitem/list relationships; focus indicators are absent.
findings.suggestedFix: Wrap primary content in main, restore sequential headings, use native disclosure semantics for FAQ, and preserve visible focus.

findings.summary: Some interactive targets fall below the inclusive 44px target recommendation.
findings.evidence: Computed pricing button size is 40x44 and login submit height is 42px; reflow itself succeeds without horizontal overflow.
findings.suggestedFix: Increase compact controls to a minimum 44x44 CSS px target area while retaining the current fluid reflow.

findings.summary: Images omit intrinsic dimensions across the sampled templates.
findings.evidence: The image primitive reports missing width/height on 13/13 homepage images and 100/100 pricing images.
findings.suggestedFix: Emit width and height (or a stable aspect-ratio) for every image so layout space is reserved before fetch completion.

findings.summary: The merge application ships incomplete source-map support.
findings.evidence: Lighthouse reports the large app.08252df.js has no source map and the mutationobserver shim map lacks sourcesContent.
findings.suggestedFix: Publish valid production source maps to the expected URLs or remove invalid sourceMappingURL references.

findings.summary: Localized pages are not connected with hreflang, and robots/sitemap requests rejected the audit client.
findings.evidence: The page exposes dozens of language routes but the pricing probe finds zero hreflang links; direct /robots.txt and /sitemap.xml requests returned 403.
findings.suggestedFix: Publish reciprocal hreflang annotations and ensure robots.txt and sitemap.xml return stable 200 responses to legitimate crawlers.

findings.summary: Rich entities have social metadata but no structured data.
findings.evidence: Homepage recon finds zero JSON-LD blocks despite organization/service content; pricing exposes plans and offers without detected structured data.
findings.suggestedFix: Add accurate schema.org Organization/WebSite and appropriate Offer/Product structured data that matches visible content.

findings.summary: The main document lacks a Content-Security-Policy and nosniff protection.
findings.evidence: The headers primitive confirms HTTPS and HSTS but no CSP and no X-Content-Type-Options; the one cookie is Secure/HttpOnly but SameSite=None.
findings.suggestedFix: Deploy a nonce/hash-based CSP and X-Content-Type-Options: nosniff; narrow cookie SameSite where cross-site use is unnecessary.

findings.summary: Google analytics requests occur before the visitor makes a consent choice.
findings.evidence: Trackers detects GTM and Google Analytics on initial load; HAR records five third-party requests and a GA collect request marked consent denied/npa=1.
findings.suggestedFix: Do not load third-party analytics before the relevant choice; prefer first-party, batched, data-minimised measurement.

findings.summary: Several browser-enforced defensive policies are absent.
findings.evidence: No clickjacking protection, Referrer-Policy, Permissions-Policy, or CSP frame-ancestors is present; HSTS is correctly enabled.
findings.suggestedFix: Add CSP frame-ancestors (and/or X-Frame-Options), strict Referrer-Policy, and a least-privilege Permissions-Policy.

findings.summary: RTL works visually, but the stylesheet relies overwhelmingly on physical directions.
findings.evidence: Arabic is correctly lang=ar and dir=rtl with no mobile overflow, yet the CSS probe counts 0 logical-property rules and 291 left/right rules.
findings.suggestedFix: Migrate layout spacing and positioning to inline/block logical properties, retaining targeted physical exceptions only where semantically required.

findings.summary: The consent prompt offers a prominent Accept all action but no equally direct Reject all action.
findings.evidence: Across screenshots, first-layer choices are Manage options and Accept all; rejecting requires additional steps while acceptance is one click.
findings.suggestedFix: Place Reject all beside Accept all with equal prominence and preserve granular management as a secondary action.

findings.summary: Login errors are not surfaced after user submission.
findings.evidence: Blank submission produces no visible field message, summary, aria-invalid state, or changed screenshot.
findings.suggestedFix: Use :user-invalid/aria-invalid after submission, clear field-level guidance, and an accessible error announcement.

findings.summary: Login fields omit autofill tokens and persistent labels.
findings.evidence: The email and password inputs return empty autocomplete values and label count 0.
findings.suggestedFix: Add visible labels plus autocomplete=username and autocomplete=current-password; retain passkey as a complementary option.

findings.summary: Homepage imagery is not consistently optimized for stable, efficient delivery.
findings.evidence: Five homepage images use PNG, five omit srcset, and every sampled image omits intrinsic dimensions, although most icons use SVG.
findings.suggestedFix: Provide responsive srcset/sizes and modern AVIF/WebP where photographic/raster content is appropriate; include intrinsic dimensions.

findings.summary: Analytics consumes a disproportionate share of a relatively light page.
findings.evidence: GTM alone transfers 165KB of the 528KB load, while all first-party scripts together are smaller; trackers also contacts Analytics.
findings.suggestedFix: Set a third-party byte budget and defer or replace analytics so it is proportional to user value and consent.

findings.summary: The PDF workflow has no structured agent-facing capability.
findings.evidence: The platform probe finds no WebMCP surface; Lighthouse agentic-browsing scores merge and pricing at 0.5, and merge’s unlabeled file input weakens the accessibility tree.
findings.suggestedFix: Expose narrowly scoped PDF operations through safe WebMCP/agentic forms with explicit file, privacy, confirmation, and output contracts.

findings.summary: Major route and workflow state changes swap abruptly without View Transition integration.
findings.evidence: The upload flow changes from picker to ordering workspace to download page; DOM/CSS inspection found no view-transition naming or transition evidence.
findings.suggestedFix: Add same-document transitions for picker/workspace state and cross-document View Transitions for result navigation, while respecting reduced motion.

taskList.title: Replace the consent wall with fair, semantic controls
Restore accessible names, landmarks, heading structure, contrast, focus, and target sizes
Deploy CSP and complete the browser security-policy baseline
Add humane login validation, labels, and autofill tokens
Improve LCP discovery and resource dependency chains
Reserve and optimize image space and formats
Add dark-mode tokens and preference-driven browser theming
Publish hreflang, crawler-stable indexing files, and structured data
Migrate RTL-sensitive layout to CSS logical properties
Add workflow View Transitions with reduced-motion handling
Expose a safe structured agent capability for PDF operations
